note: Living-book batch only. Who HQ, Ready-to-Read, and the Capstone wall graphic were verified but held off this batch because they are surveys, not stories. Events array empty.
source: Bethlehem Books; History Unboxed; Simply Charlotte Mason / Beautiful Feet / Cathy Duffy; Simon Spotlight; Penguin Random House What Was? + Common Sense Media What Was? series; Publishers Weekly + Plumfield Moms; Capstone / Bulk Bookstore ages

books.title: C is for Charlemagne
books.author: History Unboxed
books.blurb: Alphabet tour of Charlemagne—schools, crown, and court—with kid text and deeper adult notes, gentle enough for a first Middle Ages stop.

books.title: Son of Charlemagne
books.author: Barbara Willard
books.blurb: Young Carl rides to Rome with King Charles and watches his father crowned emperor—learning, family hard choices, and a vision for a united Christian West.

books.title: The Magna Charta
books.author: James Daugherty
books.blurb: Barons force King John to seal the Great Charter—a lively freedom story SCM and Beautiful Feet use in Middle Ages history.
books.parentNote: Cathy Duffy: stop around page 130 before the 1950s UN / modern-charters ending, or read those chapters with parent commentary. Used in SCM Pageant of History Middle Ages grades 5–8.

books.title: Casey Over There
books.author: Staton Rabin
books.blurb: Brooklyn boy Aubrey waits for his brother Casey, who is fighting in France, and even writes Uncle Sam—a gentle home-front door into America’s Great War.
books.parentNote: Publishers Weekly ages 4–8; Plumfield Moms notes no on-page blood or soldier deaths, but war pictures and a scare when mother fears a telegram. Read-aloud for the 6 and 8; not a cozy bedtime default for the youngest.
